sections.text: # Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: When a saturated, low-permeability soil (clay, silt) is loaded, it cannot immediately expel its pore water. The load is temporarily carried by increased pore pressure. Over time, the excess pore pressure dissipates, the effective stress increases, and the soil skeleton compresses — this is consolidation. The settlement can be large (meters for soft clay) and slow (years to decades). Understanding both magnitude and time rate is essential for foundation design.

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               CONSOLIDATION — TWO DISTINCT PROBLEMS              |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  PROBLEM 1: HOW MUCH will it settle?                            |
|  = consolidation magnitude                                       |
|  = governed by compressibility parameters (Cc, Cs)              |
|  = determined from oedometer (consolidation) test               |
|                                                                  |
|  PROBLEM 2: HOW LONG until it settles?                          |
|  = rate of consolidation                                         |
|  = governed by drainage length and permeability (Cv)            |
|  = Terzaghi's diffusion equation solution                        |
|                                                                  |
|  BOTH PROBLEMS needed for:                                       |
|  - Predicting total settlement (structural design)               |
|  - Predicting differential settlement (structural damage)        |
|  - Designing preloading schedules                                |
|  - Sizing prefabricated vertical drains                          |
|                                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

sections.text: ## The Oedometer Test

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: The fundamental lab test for consolidation behavior: a thin (2–3 cm) sample confined laterally in a rigid ring, drained at top and bottom. Load applied in increments (typically doubled: 25, 50, 100, 200, 400 kPa...).

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: For each load increment, dial gauge records settlement vs. time (Terzaghi curve for each increment).

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
**Output from oedometer**:
- e vs. log σ'v curve (compression curve)
- Cv (coefficient of consolidation) from each load increment
- Preconsolidation pressure σ'p (Casagrande construction)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ## The e - log σ' Curve

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
```
e (void ratio)
|
|  Virgin compression line (VCL)
|  (slope = Cc — compression index)
| *
|   *
|     *  ← Preconsolidation pressure σ'p (peak past stress)
|       *                                   ↓
|       |*  Recompression range            ---
|       |  * (slope = Cs — swelling index)  |
|       |    *                              Cc = Δe / Δ(log σ'v)
|       |      *                            typically 0.1–0.8
|       |    ↑  * ← Current stress σ'vo
|       | Cs/Cc ≈ 1/5 to 1/10
|       |
+─────────────────────────────── log σ'v
        σ'p  σ'vo

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
OCR = σ'p / σ'vo
  OCR = 1: normally consolidated (NC)
  OCR > 1: overconsolidated (OC) — soil has experienced higher stress in past
```

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Overconsolidation causes**: Glacial loading, erosion of overlying material, past drying/desiccation, chemical cementation.

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
**OC soils are stiffer**: They have already been compressed; recompression uses Cs (much smaller than Cc). Major practical difference:
- NC clay: uses Cc (large settlement)
- OC clay, OC region: uses Cs (small settlement)
- If new stress exceeds σ'p: uses Cs to σ'p, then Cc beyond

sections.text: ## Settlement Magnitude Calculation

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Normally Consolidated Clay (σ'f > σ'p = σ'vo)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Δe = Cc × log(σ'f / σ'vo)**

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Settlement**: Sc = (Cc / (1 + eo)) × H × log(σ'f / σ'vo)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Overconsolidated Clay — Two Cases

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
**Case 1**: Stress remains in OC range (σ'f < σ'p):
Sc = (Cs / (1 + eo)) × H × log(σ'f / σ'vo)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
**Case 2**: Stress crosses preconsolidation pressure (σ'f > σ'p):
Sc = (Cs / (1 + eo)) × H × log(σ'p / σ'vo) + (Cc / (1 + eo)) × H × log(σ'f / σ'p)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Stress Increase with Depth

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
The applied stress σ'f at depth z below a loaded area decreases with depth. Two methods:
- **2:1 method** (simplified): stress spreads at 2V:1H → Δσ'v = Q / (B+z)(L+z)
- **Boussinesq elastic solution**: more accurate for flexible loads, uses influence charts

sections.text: ## Terzaghi's 1D Consolidation Theory

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### The Governing Equation

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: For a saturated clay layer of thickness 2H (drained top and bottom), loaded at time t=0 by a uniform stress increase Δσ, Terzaghi derived the consolidation equation:

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs
Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
where:
- u = excess pore pressure (above hydrostatic) at depth z, time t
- Cv = coefficient of consolidation = k / (γw × mv)
- mv = volume compressibility = Δεv / Δσ'v = 1 / (1 + eo) × (Δe / Δσ'v)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: This is the **diffusion equation** — mathematically identical to heat conduction. The excess pore pressure diffuses from the clay (undrained interior) to the drainage boundaries (where u = 0).

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Solution: Time Factor and Degree of Consolidation

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Time Factor**: Tv = Cv × t / Hdr²

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
where Hdr = drainage length:
- Single drainage (one boundary): Hdr = H (full layer thickness)
- Double drainage (two boundaries): Hdr = H/2

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Average Degree of Consolidation** U vs. Tv:

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs
Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
**Solving for time**:
Given Sc (total settlement), want U = Sc_current / Sc_total → find Tv → solve t = Tv × Hdr² / Cv

sections.text: ## Measuring Cv from Oedometer Test

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: Two methods from the settlement vs. time curve for each load increment:

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
### Taylor's Method (√t fitting)
1. Plot settlement vs. √t
2. Early part is linear → draw line through origin
3. A line with 15% greater slope intersects the curve at t90
4. Tv at 90% consolidation = 0.848
5. Cv = 0.848 × Hdr² / t90

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
### Casagrande's Method (log t fitting)
1. Plot settlement vs. log t
2. Find t50 at the inflection point (intersection of two tangents)
3. Tv at 50% = 0.197
4. Cv = 0.197 × Hdr² / t50

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: Cv typically ranges from 0.1 to 100 m²/yr for soft to stiff clays.

sections.text: ## Piezometers and Field Monitoring

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
In the field, consolidation is tracked by:
- **Piezometers** (Casagrande, vibrating wire): measure pore pressure at specific depths
- **Settlement plates**: measure surface settlement vs. time
- **Settlement monuments**: survey points on fill surface

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
Comparing theoretical Terzaghi curves to measured pore pressure dissipation:
- Faster dissipation than predicted: better drainage than assumed (sand layers, fissures)
- Slower dissipation: smear from driving, lower k than assumed

sections.text: ## Secondary Consolidation (Creep)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: After primary consolidation (excess pore pressure fully dissipated), soil continues to compress under constant effective stress — this is secondary consolidation or creep.

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: **Cα** = secondary compression index = Δe / Δ(log t)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: Settlement rate: Ss = Cα / (1 + ep) × H × log(t2/t1)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: where ep = void ratio at end of primary consolidation.

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
Cα/Cc ≈ 0.04 ± 0.01 for inorganic clays
Cα/Cc ≈ 0.05 ± 0.01 for organic clays
Cα/Cc ≈ 0.075 ± 0.01 for peats

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
Secondary consolidation is significant for:
- Organic soils (Cα/Cc can reach 0.1)
- Long-term settlements in soft clay (decades)
- Buildings on reclaimed land

sections.text: ## Accelerating Consolidation

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Surcharge Loading

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
Apply a temporary surcharge (extra fill) beyond the final design load:
- Creates higher Δσ'v → faster consolidation
- Primary consolidation completes sooner
- Secondary consolidation time "credit" can be used
- Remove surcharge when required degree of consolidation achieved

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: ### Prefabricated Vertical Drains (PVDs)

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text: PVDs (band drains, wick drains) installed in a grid pattern to add radial drainage paths, dramatically reducing drainage path length.

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
```
PVD typically: 100mm wide × 3-5mm thick band drain
  Depth: 10-30m depending on weak layer thickness

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
Barron's radial consolidation theory:
  Tr = Cv-radial × t / de²
  where de = 1.13s (square pattern) or 1.05s (triangular)
              s = drain spacing

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
With PVDs: drainage path = half drain spacing (1-2m)
  vs. without PVDs: drainage path = half clay layer (5-15m)
  Time to 90% consolidation reduced by factor of (Hdr/re)²
  → From years to months
```

sections.text: ## Decision Cheat Sheet

metadata.title: Consolidation: Primary Settlement, Terzaghi 1D Theory, Time Rates, PVDs

sections.text:
| Design / Diagnosis Question | Use This Model | Watch-Out |
|---|---|---|
| How much will a normally consolidated clay settle? | Virgin compression line with Cc | Confirm final stress is beyond preconsolidation pressure |
| How much will an overconsolidated clay settle? | Recompression with Cs until sigma'p, then Cc if crossed | A wrong sigma'p estimate changes settlement by multiples |
| How long will settlement take? | Terzaghi time factor: t = Tv x Hdr^2 / Cv | Drainage length dominates because it is squared |
| Why is field settlement faster/slower than lab prediction? | Compare settlement plates and piezometers to theory | Sand seams, fissures, smear, and anisotropic permeability break 1D assumptions |
| Is secondary compression material? | Calpha after primary consolidation | Peat/organic clay and long service lives make creep a design issue |
| Should preloading/PVDs be used? | Radial consolidation plus staged embankment stability | Accelerating drainage does not remove the need to check undrained stability during filling |
| When can surcharge be removed? | Target U%, pore-pressure dissipation, and settlement-rate threshold | Calendar time alone is not evidence of consolidation completion |
